content: Client brief: national multi-store portal; nav Inventory · Locations · Services (Insurance, Service, PPF) · Finance · About · Contact, no Shop; SRP sticky Make/Model/Sort/Keyword, no Year; keep red, likes dark; homepage About+Locations combined (liked iBuy map), Sell Your Car no form, Reviews, IG, Services, footer location cards like CMC.

Locations: West Coast = duPont REGISTRY Select SoCal (Murrieta, CA), Naples (Select Naples), Miami (duPont REGISTRY Miami). Facts verified on dupontregistry.com 2026-10-08; Miami 615 phone and SoCal 'ET' hours still to confirm with client.

Colours mandatory: Deep Red #AC1D28, Graphite #303137 + ivory, charcoal, warm near-black, metallic. No flat pure black. Red measured from westcoastexoticcars.com (colour-only reference, pending client confirmation).
Hard rule: no paid services or credit-consuming tools (fal.ai etc.) without Alex's explicit approval; no generated imagery.

Hard rule: no blurred/feathered photo edges, vignettes, artificial shadows at image borders, dark overlays hiding integration, background extension or fake light. If an effect can't be seamless, simplify it — never degrade the photo.
Pin-stops: every pinned text beat must hold completely still and readable (≥40–60vh) before anything moves.
Project isolation: global design knowledge reusable; other clients' research, assets, data, concepts not — unless Alex authorises (he authorised Robb Francis v3 inventory behaviour).
US map at most once per page (V4 used it ~4 times). Only in About + Locations; no map crops in footer cards or decorative map silhouettes.

Active version V4 (site/v4/, live at sigovs.github.io/DUPONT). Hero: three front-facing cars together — Ferrari F430, red Ford GT centre, Porsche 911 Sport Classic — ivory studio; pinned scroll: cars advance, grow, side cars leave, Ford exits upward and the Collection rises ('The Wake').

V4 car images are temporary cut-outs; Alex will supply final professional cut-outs with alpha + shadows. Each car is an independently replaceable layer (site/v4/ASSETS.md). Don't improve temp masks or resolution.
Home inventory section uses the behaviour of Alex's Robb Francis v3 'Available Now.' — pinned scene, horizontal scroll-driven card rail, focused card larger and lit. Behaviour/layout only.
INSPIRATION/ boards (AI concepts) are a reference for layout, composition, visual rhythm and pacing — never for their pictures.
Way of working: build working prototypes early and show browser renders/recordings; no endless static storyboard/approval loops; make reasonable decisions without asking per section.
REJECTED V1 'Lights On' (dark showroom at night, 918 light-spread peak) and its SVJ hero (copied dR's marketplace hero). Soft-light/feathered peak v2 rejected outright.
REJECTED 'The Floor' hero (cars sliding onto one floor line): white photo plates on black read as dR listing cards / a slider.
REJECTED V2 'One house, three rooms' and static concepts A/B/C (edge-pixel background extension produced kinks/streaks).
REJECTED 'Head-On' (three centred frontal cars + symmetrical centreline seam): repetitive centred cars, symmetrical wipe slideshow.
REJECTED 'Step Back' storyboard: 'rearranged inventory photographs, not a premium automotive digital experience' — elaborate transitions on visually ordinary layouts.
REJECTED V4 storyboard v1 F3–F5: floating graphite aperture square, empty transition screen, white plates on graphite cards.

Lesson: dR listing photos are 124/146 bright white-cyc studio — Forge-level dark direction needs dark/detail frames (fetch more from dR listings), cut-outs staged as objects, ivory studio as aesthetic, or commissioned photography. Audit photos before choosing a direction.
DELIVERED to client 2026-10-09: https://sigovs.github.io/DUPONT/site_v1/v4/ (commit 382f1b2, tag client-delivery-2026-10-09, home page only). Baseline — never change it silently.

Manager notes 2026-10-12: too much scrolling, sections felt separate — client wants seamless access to each section; inventory must use real vehicle tiles (photos, not cut-outs) placed under the hero slider.

V3 client preview https://sigovs.github.io/DUPONT/site_v3/ (2026-10-12): continuous page 26.7 -> 10.8 screens, no pins, hero = on-load intro only; inventory under hero with listing photos, olive ground and pills unchanged, neighbours fully visible, 6px photo radius; closing rear trio kept with short entrance; Services = one 'Speak with us' button, Finance line removed. INDEX only: SRP/VDP/external links blocked.
Buttons: .02em letter-spacing everywhere — wide tracking on buttons rejected ('looks disgusting').
Change only what was asked: one note = one fix. Services pills complaint was wrongly generalised to the whole site and the inventory ground was recoloured — both reverted.
Alex 2026-10-12: he does NOT like the static V3 (site_v3) — the changes came from his manager. V3 is the manager-driven variant for the client; Alex's own direction stays the scroll-choreographed V4.

Context (Alex, 2026-10-12): the manager's 'make it static / less scrolling' note for DUPONT was most likely carried over from client comments on another project (BRAMAN Bentley / Rolls-Royce) — a newly learned term applied here, not a duPont client request. Treat the V3 static direction as a hypothesis to verify with the duPont client, not a confirmed requirement.

Fact (Alex, 2026-10-12): duPont did NOT ask for the static/less-scroll changes. The manager requested them herself ('make the changes and I'll send them to the client'). V3 = manager's own variant, sent by her to the client; not a client requirement. Supersedes the earlier 'likely carried over from BRAMAN' hypothesis.

V3 2026-10-12 (Kirsten): showroom label 'Select SoCal' -> 'Southern California' on tiles and reviews (was read as 'social'); footer keeps the official dealer name. Inventory rebuilt as proper vehicle tiles: equal graphite #303137 cards with photo, showroom, model, price, spec and 'View this car' pill inside, 4 across, row pages with arrows/drag/swipe. To review later: pill contrast on graphite; label wraps at 1280x720.
